original_record.question:
Nina made a wall around a square area, using 36 identical cubes. A section of the wall is shown in the picture. How many cubes will she now need to completely fill the square area.
<image1>
original_record.subject: combinatorial geometry

inventory.source: Five foreground vertical cube panels, top unit grid, perpendicular return-wall top grid, three visible return vertical fragments and an inner bottom continuation; deliberately omitted far-end closure retained
inventory.native_model: One shared 3D unit lattice and parallel projection; explicit world endpoints distinguish physical near-wall occlusion from schematic display truncation

answer_verification.method: For a one-cube-thick wall around an n by n outside square, boundary cubes=4n−4=36, so n=10. The unfilled interior is(n−2)^2=8^2=64 cubes. The illustration is only a section and is not falsely counted as the full wall.

audit.explicit_conditions_vs_layout: Geometry and option identity preserved. Locations and panel spacing are display layout only.

prior_triage.inventory_notes: Deliberately partial wall section: five foreground cube faces, returning wall top edges and interrupted continuation strokes. Question36 cubes around square implies10x10 outer ring and8x8 interior64. Need native3D partial-scene model, no invented full-wall depiction.
